newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Passengers at Swiss airports rise 3.9 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Passengers at Swiss airports rise 3.9 pct in 1996.

text.p: The number of passengers travelling through Swiss airports in 1996 rose 3.9 percent to more than 24.7 million, a rise that is below the average 5.6 percent rise in the last five years, the Swiss Transport Ministry said.

While Zurich's aiport gained further market share with the number of passengers rising to 5.8 percent to 15.8 million, Geneva's airport lost ground as the number of pasengers fell 0.9 percent to 6.0 million.

A higher number of passengers carried by non-Swiss carriers at Geneva's airport -- an incrase of 6.0 percent -- could not compensate for an 8.5 percent decline in passengers carried by Swiss carriers, primarily Swissair AG.
"Swiss airlines have increasingly concentrated their activities in Zurich, up 8.7 percent, or in Basle, up 11.6 percent," the ministry said.

Last year Swissair withdrew most of its intercontinental flights from Geneva in favour of the Zurich hub. The move was not only heavily criticised by Geneva politicians, but members of the federal government also expressed their dissatisfaction.
Foreign airlines have also pulled back from Swiss regional airports, such as Berne and Lugano, and let Swiss airlines serve these airports, the ministry added.
